# Shaders std vocabulary (engine 4.0.4)

Compose shaders from these words with `defineShader` from `shaders/std`. Every word is a plain TypeScript
function; the engine lowers the composition to WGSL at runtime. A `wgsl` body is the escape hatch.

## Defining a shader

### defineShader & wgsl (`shaders/std` top level) — https://shaders.com/docs/primitives/define

A shader is a plain object: a name, the props a user can set, and one field that says what it
draws. Hand it to `defineShader` and it becomes a component you can mount, nest, blend, mask
and animate like any shader in the library.

- `defineShader<T extends ComponentProps>(definition: StdDefinition<T>): GpuShaderDefinition<T>` — Define a shader component from a plain object: its props, and one field that says what it draws.
- `wgsl(spec: WgslSpec): WgslBody
wgsl(body: string): WgslBody
wgsl(strings: TemplateStringsArray, ...values: unknown[]): WgslBody` — Write the per-pixel math by hand, as one WGSL function body that returns a `vec4f` color.
- `registerShader<T extends GpuShaderDefinition<any>>(definition: T): T` — Make a user-defined shader findable by its `name`, so preset JSON can reference it as `type: 'Halo'`.
- `unregisterShader(name: string): void` — Forget a user-defined shader by name.
- `getRegisteredShader(name: string): GpuShaderDefinition | undefined` — Look up a user-defined shader by name.
- `getRegisteredShaders(): GpuShaderDefinition[]` — Every user-defined shader currently registered, oldest first.
- `onShaderRegistered(listener: (name: string, definition: GpuShaderDefinition | null) => void): () => void` — Be told when a user-defined shader is registered, replaced or removed.
- `class WgslBody` — What `wgsl` returns: a body ready to sit in `paint:` or `effect:`.

### Props & values (`shaders/std` top level) — https://shaders.com/docs/primitives/values

How a definition points at its own props. `p('radius')` is a **prop ref**: hand it to any word
that takes a color, a position or a number and the word reads that prop live on the GPU, with
drivers and animation applied, and no rebuild when the value changes. A **Scalar** is a number
built from props and masks. `radialMask(…)` returns one, so does `oscillating(…)` from
`motion`, and `.times(p('intensity'))` scales one by a prop. Words that take a `ScalarInput`
accept either a prop ref or a Scalar.

- `p(name: string): PropRef` — Reference one of the definition's props by name, wherever a word asks for a value.
- `class Scalar` — A number built from props: what `radialMask(…)`, `motion.oscillating(…)` and `.times()` return.

### Identity & recompile rules (`shaders/std` top level) — https://shaders.com/docs/primitives/slots

Two small kinds of rule that make a filter cheap. An **identity rule** sits on a filter
definition's `identityWhen:` and says when the filter does nothing: while it holds, the layer
inside passes through untouched and the effect costs no GPU time. A **recompile rule** sits
on a prop's `recompile:` and says which changes rebuild the shader rather than just update a
value.

- `crosses(value: number): RecompileRule` — Rebuild the shader only when the prop crosses `value`, not on every change.
- `isZero(prop: string): IdentityRule` — Skip the filter entirely while `prop` is exactly 0.
- `isValue(prop: string, value: unknown): IdentityRule` — Skip the filter entirely while `prop` equals `value`, for a filter whose no-op is not 0.
- `allOf(...rules: IdentityRule[]): IdentityRule` — Skip the filter only while every rule holds, for a no-op that needs several props at rest.
- `identityWhenever(props: string[], when: (values: Record<string, unknown>) => boolean): IdentityRule` — Skip the filter when your own test of the props' values says so.
- `recompileWhen(predicate: (prev: any, next: any) => boolean): RecompileRule` — Rebuild when your own test of the old and new value says so, for a threshold `crosses` cannot express.

### Context & invocation (`shaders/std` top level) — https://shaders.com/docs/primitives/invoke

The **context** is what every pixel knows about its surroundings: its coordinate (`uv`, 0–1
across the canvas with y down), the clock (`time`, in seconds), the canvas shape (`aspect`,
`viewportSize`) and the mouse (`pointer`). `ctx` names these as tokens you can pass to a word
or bind in a `wgsl` body's `inputs`.

- `ctx.uv: CtxToken` — The pixel's coordinate: 0–1 across the canvas, y down.
- `ctx.time: CtxToken` — The global clock in seconds.
- `ctx.aspect: CtxToken` — The canvas's width divided by its height.
- `ctx.pointer: CtxToken` — The mouse position in uv (0–1, y down).
- `ctx.viewportSize: CtxToken` — The frame size in device pixels, as a `vec2f`.
- `ctx.logicalViewportSize: CtxToken` — The frame size in CSS pixels, as a `vec2f`, for feature counts that should not change with screen density.
- `paintFrame(params: GpuFragmentParams): {uv: Expr; viewport: Expr}` — The coordinate and

on a prop's `recompile:` and says which changes rebuild the shader rather than just update a

- `crosses(value: number): RecompileRule` — Rebuild the shader only when the prop crosses `value`, not on every change.
- `isZero(prop: string): IdentityRule` — Skip the filter entirely while `prop` is exactly 0.
- `isValue(prop: string, value: unknown): IdentityRule` — Skip the filter entirely while `prop` equals `value`, for a filter whose no-op is not 0.
- `allOf(...rules: IdentityRule[]): IdentityRule` — Skip the filter only while every rule holds, for a no-op that needs several props at rest.
- `identityWhenever(props: string[], when: (values: Record<string, unknown>) => boolean): IdentityRule` — Skip the filter when your own test of the props' values says so.
- `recompileWhen(predicate: (prev: any, next: any) => boolean): RecompileRule` — Rebuild when your own test of the old and new value says so, for a threshold `crosses` cannot express.

The **context** is what every pixel knows about its surroundings: its coordinate (`uv`, 0–1

- `ctx.uv: CtxToken` — The pixel's coordinate: 0–1 across the canvas, y down.

export interface ShaderOptions {
    /**
     * User-defined components (`defineShader(...)` results from `shaders/std`) this preset may
     * reference by `type`. Components registered globally with `registerShader` are found too.
     */
    components?: import('../core').GpuShaderDefinition[];
    colorSpace?: 'p3-linear' | 'srgb';
    toneMapping?: 'linear' | 'reinhard' | 'cineon' | 'aces' | 'agx' | 'neutral' | 'hable' | 'unreal';
    disableTelemetry?: boolean;
    enablePerformanceTracking?: boolean;
    isPreview?: boolean;
    onReady?: () => void;
    /**
     * Fires when something goes wrong with the GPU. Two flavours:
     *
     * **Recoverable** — the device was lost (Chrome evicting a backgrounded tab's
     * WebGPU device, an OS-level GPU reset, a driver crash). By the time this runs
     * the instance has already started rebuilding itself transparently against the
     * same canvas and preset; your existing `update / pause / resume / resize /
     * destroy` references keep working once the rebuild completes. Informational —
     * surface a toast, write a log, no action required. `reason` is a best-effort
     * string from the underlying API.
     *
     * **Terminal** — the shader will never draw and has released everything. The
     * canvas is left as-is (transparent, if it never rendered). This is the moment
     * to swap in a static fallback. `reason` is one of:
     *
     * - `'unsupported'`    — the browser has no WebGPU at all
     * - `'no-adapter'`     — WebGPU exists but no GPU adapter was granted
     * - `'no-device'`      — an adapter exists but the device request failed
     * - `'init-failed'`    — start-up threw for some other reason
     * - `'device-lost'`    — lost with no recovery possible
     * - `'out-of-memory'`  — the GPU refused an allocation
     * - `'gpu-error'`      — sustained device errors; the GPU is not usable
     * - `'render-failed'`  — repeated exceptions while composing or drawing
     * - `'limit-exceeded'` — the composition needs more of some GPU resource than this device
     *                        allows (today: more uniform bytes than a single binding permits).
     *                        Unlike the others this is about the CONTENT — fewer layers would run
     * - `'unrecoverable'`  — too many device losses in a row; we stopped retrying
     * - `'rebuild_failed'` — a device-loss rebuild itself failed
     *
     * A terminal reason is reported exactly once. Check {@link isWebGPUSupported} or
     * `getWebGPUSupport()` before mounting if you'd rather not create the shader at
     * all on an unsupported browser.
     */
    onError?: (reason: string) => void;

     *

     *  const shader = await createShader(canvas, preset, {
     *    observeElement: false
     *  })
     *

aiTitle: Lenis scroll and conversational persona chat

content.thinking:
The full-page screenshot confirms the reveals aren't firing yet since they only trigger on intersection, which makes sense given wardrobe cards, method steps, and the QD archive are missing. Now I'm sketching a concrete plan, starting with adding Lenis smooth scrolling in the layout with reduced-motion support and anchor link handling.

I want Lenis to drive the Reveal component's scroll-progress behavior, excluding the Studio route since it has inner scrollable panes that need `data-lenis-prevent`. Beyond that, I'm thinking about richer scroll-linked effects — a pinned horizontal "method" track, word-by-word headline reveals, and velocity-based skew on a marquee — implemented with GSAP's ScrollTrigger paired with Lenis, since GSAP is already installed and now fully free to use.

Next I'm turning to the conversational AI chat interface, thinking through how to make it feel more engaging while explaining the persona, design, and flow.

I'm picturing the public-facing chat as a real conversation with a persona character (like the Cyberbotanist) who speaks in first person about their taste and design choices, or a "tailor" host explaining the Baste flow — complete with typing indicators, portraits, and suggested replies. On the backend, I'd build a `/api/chat` endpoint with a persona-based system prompt and SSE streaming, but I also need an honest, scripted fallback conversation engine from persona data (keyword-matched intents) for when there's no server or API key, since the site may deploy statically and PRODUCT.md requires the demo not misrepresent itself.

I'm thinking the site should split audience-friendly content from technical content: the homepage becomes a narrative-driven experience with a hero, simplified measurement section, "meet the personas" chat, wardrobe, and closing, while judge weights, QD archive, deliverables, and install commands move to a dedicated page like `/method` or `/how` ("Inside the method" / "Under the hood"), separate from the existing `/docs`.

I also want to check whether there's already a chat component in the studio by grepping the site code and looking at git diffs, since the user mentioned prior design attempts that got deleted. For the WebGPU shaders, I'm planning to wrap vanilla shader creation in a Qwik `ShaderCanvas` component with a static fallback, using it as live backdrops behind each persona's chat header — bioluminescent ink-flow for the cyberbotanist, thread strands, CRT/VHS for the liminal weeb persona, and neon glitch for the nightmarket coder.

I still need to understand the preset JSON component tree format, including nested components and effects that distort layers below, so I should check the docs or llms reference for that structure. For react-bits, since Qwik can't consume React components directly, I'll port the logic of specific pieces like SplitText/BlurText and ScrollVelocity marquee rather than use them as-is, treating it as legitimate since react-bits is designed to be copy-paste code anyway.

Since the library favors copying source directly, I'll fetch the actual source files from DavidHDev/react-bits on GitHub to faithfully port ScrollReveal, ScrollVelocity, BlurText, and possibly Magnet into Qwik equivalents. Separately, I need to audit cursor behavior — the needle cursor only applies when ThreadCursor mounts via a data attribute on html, so I should check whether the /gui route's layout actually includes that component.

I'm finding real inconsistencies: Panda's utility layer sets explicit `cursor: pointer` on many elements, overriding the custom pin cursor and reverting to the system hand pointer. items.text: The restart stopped the local API. I’m bringing it back and finishing the docs checks: both languages, video playback and seeking, mobile layout, and links from the old developer sections.

The restored guide now has 24 Studio chapters, separate developer docs, and all three recordings. The production build passes. I’ve also checked playback, seeking, captions, and the restored media files; I’m finishing the language switches and mobile deep links.

use the fal key for producing the voice for the video walkthrough. I think we should also be adding voice as an important modality here for talking to the agent subsequent animations for that animations for the agent when speaking, when paused indications for that are very useful.
ral k ey is in  skate

I’ll use the existing fal key to narrate the walkthrough, keeping the voice consistent with the published tours. I’ll also add voice controls to the companion chat, with clear listening, thinking, speaking, and paused states, plus an obvious way to stop playback.
I’ll retrieve the fal key from Skate without exposing it. I’m using the HyperFrames and media-use workflows for narration, and keeping the voice controls within the companion’s existing design.

I found `fal_api_key` in Skate. The recovered design plan also calls for animation tied to audible playback. I’m adding tap-to-talk and spoken replies with listening, preparing, speaking, and paused states; pausing the audio will stop the speaking animation too.

fal rejected the narration request with `User is locked. Reason: TOP_UP.` The key is present, but the account needs credit before it can generate audio. I’ll continue building and testing the voice interface while that’s resolved.

The voice controls are wired up. Recording is tap-to-start and tap-to-finish, with an editable transcript before sending. Spoken replies are opt-in, and microphone and playback activity drive the companion indicator. Switching characters or leaving the tab releases the microphone and stops playback.

The browser checks confirm pause/resume, stopped animation while paused, microphone cleanup, and editable transcripts without automatic sending. The new API tests pass too. I’m testing successful playback with an existing recording and a mock provider response; new fal audio is still blocked by the account’s balance.

fal requires a balance top-up before it will generate the walkthrough narration. Let me know when the account is funded so I can retry.
I’ve topped up fal; retry
I’ll retry fal now. Once the narration is generated, I’ll align it with the five walkthrough steps and check the captions and playback.

so the fal generation needs to get done with full demonstrationns of the wonderful abilities of baste. what it is like to use it and why you would. i also hate the ugly cards in the landing page.  the different ones could be way better and appeal greatly to designers, right now they seem sloppy
I'll catch up on what happened in the earlier runs before changing anything.

/**

 * fitting renders in the persona's real faces rather than a fallback.
 * Keep in sync with TOKEN_FONT_FAMILIES on the engine side.

const PERSONA_FAMILIES = [
  "Archivo+Black",
  "Bricolage+Grotesque:opsz,wght@12..96,400..800",
  "Chakra+Petch:wght@400;600;700",
  "Dela+Gothic+One",
  "Fira+Code:wght@400;500",
  "Fraunces:ital,opsz,wght@0,9..144,300..900;1,9..144,300..900",

  "JetBrains+Mono:wght@400;500",
  "Monoton",
  "Source+Serif+4:opsz,wght@8..60,400..700",
  "Space+Mono:wght@400;700",
  "VT323",
];

export const PERSONA_FONTS_HREF =
  "https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?" +
  PERSONA_FAMILIES.map((f) => `family=${f}`).join("&") +
  "&display=swap";

/** First family name in a CSS font stack, unquoted: "'Fraunces', serif" → "Fraunces". */
export function primaryFamily(stack: string | undefined): string {
  if (!stack) return "";
  return stack.split(",")[0].trim().replace(/^['"]|['"]$/g, "");
}

Base directory for this skill: /home/diogenes/.claude/skills/hyperframes

**Plugin installs:** Before setup or freshness commands, follow [plugin execution rules](references/plugin-installation.md) when this skill is inside a HyperFrames plugin. Standalone installs keep the update instructions below.

# HyperFrames entry point

### Check remaining usage

At the start of creation, run `npx hyperframes usage --json`. Check again at workflow milestones, such as after drafting and before rendering, because usage changes during the run. Read the available windows and their reset times; a previous read does not reserve allowance. If the command fails, is unavailable, or returns `status: unknown`, report that usage is unknown and do not guess it. Keep scope and workflow choices with the user.

HyperFrames **renders video from HTML** — a composition is an HTML file whose DOM declares timing with `data-*` attributes, whose animation runtime is seekable, and whose media playback is owned by the framework. The full authoring contract lives in `/hyperframes-core`; read it before writing composition HTML. Brief, storyboard, review, production, dispatch, and frame-worker contracts live in this skill's `references/`.

## 1. Start from project state

Apply the first matching row; do not evaluate lower state rows:

Skip the intent layer.                                                                                                                      |

When you edit an existing project, bracket your edits with project history (`/hyperframes-cli`, Project history in your turn).

<!-- /history (trial) -->

If a fresh request does not identify the subject or input, ask what the video is about before routing. Check preferences and recipes before asking anything (`references/intent-interview.md`, step 1). A `figma.com` input or a named recipe changes intake, not routing — the interview's "Adapt orthogonal inputs" section handles both.

### Keep the project's CLI current

A scaffolded project pins `hyperframes@<version>` in its `package.json` scripts so renders stay reproducible; the pin never advances on its own, and a pinned run of an older CLI prints no warning about it. When resuming a project whose scripts carry a pin, probe once before the first render-affecting command:

```bash
npx hyperframes@latest upgrade --project . --check
```

The probe is read-only and reports the pin against the latest release; keep the explicit `.` — on older CLI releases a bare `--project` followed by another flag consumes that flag as its directory value. When it reports the project behind — or any CLI output already shows it (the stderr notice `This project pins hyperframes@… (latest …)`, or `_meta.updateAvailable: true` in a `--json` result from a pinned script) — apply with `npx hyperframes@latest upgrade --project .`, then verify with `npx hyperframes check`. A passing check confirms the project's compositions still validate on the new version — not that rendered output is frame-identical to the old pin — so a successful bump is never silent: name the old and new version in the run's summary. A project with no composition yet needs no verification. If the check fails, revert the `package.json` change, continue on the pinned version, and report which version the project stays on and why. Act on the signal rather than relaying it to the user; never leave a bumped pin unverified.

## 2. Route fresh creation

Use the first matching row. Match the requested **deliverable**, not a word or file type mentioned in passing.

| Priority | Request                                                                                                            | Workflow                   |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------- |
| 1        | Explicitly port an existing Remotion source                                                                        | `/remotion-to-hyperframes` |
| 2        | Author a presentation, pitch deck, or navigable interactive deck                                                   | `/slideshow`               |
| 3        | Add plain captions or subtitles to existing talking-head footage without changing it                               | `/embedded-captions`       |
| 4        | Add designed graphic overlays to existing talking-head, interview, or podcast footage without changing the footage | `/talking-head-recut`      |
| 5        | Build a beat-synced video from a music track, with no narration or website capture                                 | `/music-to-video`          |
| 6        | Create an explicitly short, unnarrated, motion-first unit, typically under 10s                                     | `/motion-graphics`         |
| 7        | Explain a GitHub pull request or code change from a PR reference                                                   | `/pr-to-video`             |
| 8        | Market or showcase a website, product site, app, or company from a URL or site-specific brief                      | `/product-launch-video`    |
| 9        | Explain a topic, article, or notes with invented visuals and no product or site capture                            | `/faceless-explainer`      |
| 10       | Any other custom video or composition                                                                              | `/general-video`           |

Before finalizing the route, read `references/routes/<workflow>.md` — one small file per route: the canonical input/output/trigger contract (available before lazy-installed workflow skills are present) plus that route's interview entry. If the candidate does not satisfy its contract, continue routing instead of forcing the match. Read only the matched route's file.

### Resolve common ambiguities

- A short animated title, logo sting, stat hit, chart hit, map hit, or standalone lower-third is `/motion-graphics` when it is unnarrated and motion is the message. A static title card, narrated sequence, longer montage, or custom loop is `/general-video`.
- An explicitly short motion graphic may use a URL, tweet, article, or screenshot as source material. A generic "make a video from this site" request is `/product-launch-video`.
- Existing footage with captions routes to `/embedded-captions`; footage with designed information cards routes to `/talking-head-recut`. Retiming, reordering, recoloring, reframing, or remixing footage is a custom edit and falls through to `/general-video`.
- A music file selects `/music-to-video` only when its beat grid drives the piece. Music used as a bed does not override the subject-matched route.
- "I want a storyboard" changes the review process, not the workflow. With no other routing signal, use `/general-video`. A confirmed sketched `storyboard.html` may itself be the requested deliverable; the review loop defines that stop point.
- Specialized narrative workflows support up to about 3 minutes and are strongest around 30–90s. Route a clearly longer piece to `/general-video`. Length never overrides an explicit port, deck, caption, overlay, or music-driven deliverable.

## 3. Route once, then leave

For fresh creation the intent layer (`references/intent-interview.md`) runs the full conversation — memory, triage, pitch round, must-haves, run-shape, hand-off — and **ends by writing `BRIEF.md`. The brief is the only routing artifact the workflow reads**; nothing later re-opens this skill or the interview. Answer every later "what did the route require?" from `BRIEF.md`.

## 4. Install and enter the workflow

Before reading the selected workflow, install or refresh it and the core domain skills:

```bash
npx hyperframes skills update <workflow-name>
```

Use the bare name without `/`. If the command fails, surface the error; do not reconstruct the workflow from memory. Everything else about installation — the core-vs-lazy split, what `init` refreshes, diagnosis, CI opt-out, and the no-CLI fallback — lives in `references/skill-lifecycle.md`.

## 5. Load domain skills on demand

| Need                                                                                                                                        | Skill                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| Composition structure, timing attributes, tracks, variables, determinism                                                                    | `/hyperframes-core`      |
| Motion rules, scene blueprints, transitions, runtime adapters                                                                               | `/hyperframes-animation` |
| Seek-safe GSAP, CSS, Anime.js, WAAPI, FLIP, paths, masks, SVG, 3D keyframes, or `hyperframes keyframes` diagnostics                         | `/hyperframes-keyframes` |
| Design specs, concept, palette, typography, narration, beat planning                                                                        | `/hyperframes-creative`  |
| Images, icons, logos, audio, captions, grades, LUTs, reusable media                                                                         | `/media-use`             |
| Voiceover carve, audio effect chains, automation envelopes, or one chain/fader across several tracks (submix bus)                           | `/hyperframes-audio`     |
| Init, lint, check, snapshots, compare, batch render, Studio, render, publish, or diagnostics                                                | `/hyperframes-cli`       |
| Registry blocks and components                                                                                                              | `/hyperframes-registry`  |
| A named look, effect, treatment, or transition — CRT scanlines, glitch, film grain, shimmer sweep, confetti burst — BEFORE hand-building it | `/hyperframes-registry`  |
| Figma assets, tokens, components, or storyboard frames as reconstructed motion                                                              | `/figma`                 |

Creator edit phrases are cross-domain requests. Load every skill named in the matching row:

| Creator request                                                                                                    | Required domains                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| “cut this footage”, hard cut, trim, splice, reorder, or use a source range                                         | `/general-video` + `/hyperframes-core`; core owns `data-start`, `data-duration`, `data-media-start`, and track layout.                                                            |
| zoom in here, punch-in / punch-out, smooth multi-state zoom or reframe, Ken Burns, or camera move                  | `/general-video` + `/hyperframes-core` + `/hyperframes-keyframes`; animate the inner visual/crop wrapper, not the timed clip.                                                     |
| match cut or whip pan camera transition                                                                            | `/general-video` + `/hyperframes-animation` + `/hyperframes-keyframes` + `/hyperframes-registry`; search/install a transition primitive before hand-authoring.                    |
| fade, crossfade, track gain/volume, automation, duck/carve, audio effects, or one effect across several tracks     | `/general-video` + `/hyperframes-core` + `/hyperframes-audio`; core places clips, audio mixes placed tracks — including a submix bus over a group of them.                        |
| picture and sound edits that combine cuts with camera motion or mixing                                             | `/general-video` + `/hyperframes-core` + `/hyperframes-keyframes` when there is visual motion + `/hyperframes-audio` when sound is faded, mixed, ducked, automated, or processed. |
| lay out a project so it reads well in Studio: caption track, tracks per element kind, sub-compositions, safe zones | `/hyperframes-studio` + `/hyperframes-core`; studio owns the layout conventions, core owns each edit.                                                                             |
| source or generate media, or preprocess an unsupported mid-source freeze                                           | `/media-use`; sourcing/generation/preprocessing only, never placed-track mixing.                                                                                                  |

Constant `data-playback-rate` is render-safe for picture and pitch-preserved
sound. Speed ramps are a `rate` lane in `data-automation`.
For copyable edit contracts, load `/hyperframes-core` → `references/creator-editing-recipes.md`.

Broad feedback about how photographic media looks or behaves also routes to

existing canonical treatment primitive. Keep text/layout/motion-only edits in
their owning domain.
During a build with important photographic media, include one grounded
media-polish scan in the final quality pass; leaving suitable media unchanged is
a valid result.

Domain skills never take ownership of the end-to-end deliverable. Load only what the active workflow needs.

1	# The intent layer — one conversation, before any workflow runs
2	
3	Fresh creation only — the SKILL.md state table already decides whether this layer runs at all (edits, project operations, briefed and resumable projects, and explicit Remotion ports never enter it). One conversation at the front door turns "make me a video" into a confirmed brief — the route, the must-have answers, the run's shape, and everything else in the user's head — handed to whichever workflow executes and made durable as `BRIEF.md`. Workflows own execution; this layer owns understanding. Every workflow's opening rule points back here, so the questions are asked once no matter which door the user came through.
4	
5	The one exception: a follow-on to the same film (a new version or a cutdown) asked for inside an existing project runs this layer as `/hyperframes-studio` § 5 describes, without `hyperframes init` and without overwriting the project's brief.
6	
7	These reads are mandatory when their condition matches; do not replace them with recollection:
8	
9	| Condition                                                   | Read before acting                                                   |
10	| ----------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
11	| The route is picked, before confirming or interviewing      | `routes/<workflow>.md` — the whole file (contract + interview, ~1KB) |
12	| Triage judged the request unformed, before any concept work | `pitch-round.md`                                                     |
13	| Offering optional capabilities or collecting supplied media | The route-filtered rows in `capability-menu.md`                      |
14	| Question rules or field semantics beyond the schema below   | `brief-contract.md`                                                  |
15	
16	## Adapt orthogonal inputs first
17	
18	A Figma source changes **how assets and design enter the project**, not which workflow owns the deliverable. If any input is a `figma.com` URL: complete this layer's memory and recipe reads; during input triage run `/figma` to extract assets, brand tokens, components, and storyboard frames when present; route the requested deliverable using the output from `/figma`, then continue only the selected route's unanswered questions. Do not drive Figma through raw MCP tools — that bypasses SVG sanitization, `.media/manifest.jsonl` provenance, and brand-token `var()` binding.
19	
20	A GitHub PR URL is not a website source. A named or adopted recipe already carries its workflow; confirm adoption below, then route to that workflow.
21	
22	## The eight steps
23	
24	**1 — Memory before questions.** Two reads, both mandatory, before anything is asked:
25	
26	- **Remembered defaults.** Let `<MEDIA_DIR>` be the installed `/media-use` skill directory. For an existing project, `<MEMORY_ROOT>` is its root. Before scaffolding, use a deliberately nonexistent probe path with no `.media`, such as `/tmp/hyperframes-intent-memory-<run-id>`; never use the current workspace. Run `node <MEDIA_DIR>/scripts/prefs.mjs get --hyperframes <MEMORY_ROOT> --json`. Make each remembered value the recommended option and name its source. The pre-project probe sees only the personal tier; do not claim project provenance.
27	- **Recipes.** Run `node <MEDIA_DIR>/scripts/recipe.mjs list --hyperframes <MEMORY_ROOT> --json`. If the user names a recipe, says "like last time," or a recipe matches the probable route, ask whether to adopt it before other brief questions — and make the offer earn the yes: say why it matches and what adopting saves ("this matches your launch-promo recipe — adopting fills destination, aspect, language, and the design spec; you'd confirm the message and the two run-shape questions"). When several match, list them and include "none." An adopted recipe locks the fields it contains; ask only its missing fields and the run-shape questions. It does not remove review or render approval gates.
28	
29	**2 — Triage the input.** What is the video about — a website (sold or shown), a PR, a topic, a music track, existing footage? And is the request **formed** — the message, the material, and the occasion readable from what the user gave — or **unformed**, a subject with no take on it? Source material doesn't settle this by itself: a site, document, or PR carries its own thesis, but five tellings of that thesis are five different videos — a request whose only shape comes from its source ("make a video about this URL") is formed about the facts and unformed about the telling, and enters the round to pitch the telling. A formed request runs the layer exactly as it always has; nothing below is added for it. # The intent layer — one conversation, before any workflow runs

Fresh creation only — the SKILL.md state table already decides whether this layer runs at all (edits, project operations, briefed and resumable projects, and explicit Remotion ports never enter it). One conversation at the front door turns "make me a video" into a confirmed brief — the route, the must-have answers, the run's shape, and everything else in the user's head — handed to whichever workflow executes and made durable as `BRIEF.md`. Workflows own execution; this layer owns understanding. Every workflow's opening rule points back here, so the questions are asked once no matter which door the user came through.

The one exception: a follow-on to the same film (a new version or a cutdown) asked for inside an existing project runs this layer as `/hyperframes-studio` § 5 describes, without `hyperframes init` and without overwriting the project's brief.

These reads are mandatory when their condition matches; do not replace them with recollection:

| Condition                                                   | Read before acting                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The route is picked, before confirming or interviewing      | `routes/<workflow>.md` — the whole file (contract + interview, ~1KB) |
| Triage judged the request unformed, before any concept work | `pitch-round.md`                                                     |
| Offering optional capabilities or collecting supplied media | The route-filtered rows in `capability-menu.md`                      |
| Question rules or field semantics beyond the schema below   | `brief-contract.md`                                                  |

## Adapt orthogonal inputs first

A Figma source changes **how assets and design enter the project**, not which workflow owns the deliverable. If any input is a `figma.com` URL: complete this layer's memory and recipe reads; during input triage run `/figma` to extract assets, brand tokens, components, and storyboard frames when present; route the requested deliverable using the output from `/figma`, then continue only the selected route's unanswered questions. Do not drive Figma through raw MCP tools — that bypasses SVG sanitization, `.media/manifest.jsonl` provenance, and brand-token `var()` binding.

A GitHub PR URL is not a website source. A named or adopted recipe already carries its workflow; confirm adoption below, then route to that workflow.

## The eight steps

**1 — Memory before questions.** Two reads, both mandatory, before anything is asked:

- **Remembered defaults.** Let `<MEDIA_DIR>` be the installed `/media-use` skill directory. For an existing project, `<MEMORY_ROOT>` is its root. Before scaffolding, use a deliberately nonexistent probe path with no `.media`, such as `/tmp/hyperframes-intent-memory-<run-id>`; never use the current workspace. Run `node <MEDIA_DIR>/scripts/prefs.mjs get --hyperframes <MEMORY_ROOT> --json`. Make each remembered value the recommended option and name its source. The pre-project probe sees only the personal tier; do not claim project provenance.
- **Recipes.** Run `node <MEDIA_DIR>/scripts/recipe.mjs list --hyperframes <MEMORY_ROOT> --json`. If the user names a recipe, says "like last time," or a recipe matches the probable route, ask whether to adopt it before other brief questions — and make the offer earn the yes: say why it matches and what adopting saves ("this matches your launch-promo recipe — adopting fills destination, aspect, language, and the design spec; you'd confirm the message and the two run-shape questions"). When several match, list them and include "none." An adopted recipe locks the fields it contains; ask only its missing fields and the run-shape questions. It does not remove review or render approval gates.

**2 — Triage the input.** What is the video about — a website (sold or shown), a PR, a topic, a music track, existing footage? And is the request **formed** — the message, the material, and the occasion readable from what the user gave — or **unformed**, a subject with no take on it? Source material doesn't settle this by itself: a site, document, or PR carries its own thesis, but five tellings of that thesis are five different videos — a request whose only shape comes from its source ("make a video about this URL") is formed about the facts and unformed about the telling, and enters the round to pitch the telling. A formed request runs the layer exactly as it always has; nothing below is added for it. Their answer seeds the round (`pitch-round.md`). A user who says they don't know video at all gets that reference's decision map instead of a question sequence. The user hears the process before any workflow starts.

The chosen concept answers the route's pitch-eligible fields and lands in `BRIEF.md` under `## Intent`; the capabilities it named are confirmed with it, under `## Customizations`.

When a diagram or source material summarizes the outcomes as three branches, that is the derived behavior (`brief-contract.md` § 1), not the question shape. A storyboard request, however phrased, locks `storyboard: yes`. Remembered `flow` / `storyboard` values reorder the recommendations — they never make either question disappear. The run's collaborative/autonomous execution mode derives from these two answers — the old first question is never asked; the canonical mapping is `brief-contract.md` § 1.

**7 — Nice-to-have: recommend, then show.** Skip this step when the selected route file says to skip the front-door capability offer. Otherwise, once the must-haves are locked, send one offer, not an interrogation — recommendations first, catalog on request. Capabilities the chosen pitch already named are settled with the concept — this step recommends from what the pitch didn't cover, and after a pitch round it is often just the two open asks and the design ask:

# Fitting loop — Baste hero motion

**Deliverables:** `renders/fitting-loop.mp4` (1200×630, 30fps, 8.0s, seamless loop) and
`renders/fitting-loop.gif` (960×504, 15fps, ≤ 4 MB, palette-optimised via ffmpeg palettegen/paletteuse)
plus a 1200×630 PNG still at t=1.6s → `renders/og-baste.png` (this replaces site/public/og-baste.png).

**What it says, without words:** one interface, cut three times. The same app screen is re-fitted
to three personas using their real generated tokens; nothing else changes.

## House style (the frame around the garment)
- Ground: pattern paper `#F1ECE2` with a 32px drafting grid `rgba(28,27,25,0.05)`.
- Ink `#1C1B19`, ink-muted `#6E6A61`, basting thread `#D2402A`, tailor's chalk `#2F55A4`, tape `#F0C534`.
- Faces (Google Fonts): Bodoni Moda (display, italic for the wordmark), IBM Plex Mono (chalk notes),
  plus each persona's faces below.

## Layout (1200×630)
- Left column (x 64–420): wordmark "Baste" Bodoni Moda italic 600, 56px, ink. Under it, two lines, Bodoni Moda 30px:
  "Cut to fit" / "*one* person." (*one* italic in `#A9311E`). Under that a 1.5px basting rule (12px dash / 8px gap, thread red).
  Bottom-left: mono 13px ink-muted "persona → tokens → interface".
- Centre (x 450–960): a bolt of cloth (rotated −1.6°, pinked/zig-zag top+bottom edge, soft drop shadow) dyed in the
  current persona's primary over its background as a visible plain weave: CSS `repeating-linear-gradient` warp
  (primary, 3px on / 3px off) over weft (background, 3px/3px) at 90°, with a subtle diagonal light gradient for folds.
  On it, pinned with two red pin heads (radial gradient #F38A74→#D2402A→#8E2615), the **garment card** (≈470×360):
  window chrome row (3 dots in primary/secondary/accent + mono "<id>.app / collections"), eyebrow (mono, primary,
  uppercase), heading (persona heading font, 34px, the persona's obsession), two buttons ("Start a collection" filled
  primary; "Browse" ghost), a "Pinned spaces" surface listing 3 spaces with coloured bullets, a "Now playing" surface
  (artist in heading font, genre muted, progress bar in primary), and 3 keyword chips. Card bg = persona background,
  surfaces = persona surface, borders = persona border, radii from persona tokens (radius.xl on card, radius.base on buttons),
  padding: minimal 26px / rich 20px / maximalist 12px.
- Right column (x 990–1160): chalk notes, mono 12px, each with a 1.5px dashed chalk left border:
  DISPLAY FACE <heading family> · PRIMARY <swatch + hex> · RADIUS <base · edge> · DENSITY <density>.

## Persona data (exact)
1. cyberbotanist — eyebrow "Pacific Northwest"; heading "Mycelial network topology"; spaces greenhouses, herbariums,
   maker spaces with plants; artist Biosphere / ambient; chips Mushishi, Ernst Haeckel, bioluminescent.
   primary #a15d3f secondary #5a8e3f accent #35f3b5 bg #fdf1eb surface #fffbf9 border #dacec9 text #211815 muted #685a54.
   heading 'Fraunces' (700), body 'Source Serif 4'. radius base 12px, xl 32px. density rich. edge organic.
2. nightmarketcoder — eyebrow "East Asian metropolitan"; heading "Point-of-sale systems"; spaces night markets,
   convenience stores at 2am, rooftops; artist Mariya Takeuchi / city pop; chips Chungking Express, night markets, neon signage.
   primary #e44635 secondary #ebb230 accent #fe12a9 bg #150d0c surface #211816 border #3a302e text #f5ecea muted #b1a09d.
   heading 'Dela Gothic One', body 'Instrument Sans'. radius base 4px, xl 12px. density maximalist. edge geometric.
3. liminalweeb — eyebrow "Digital native"; heading "Lost media"; spaces abandoned malls, empty pools, server rooms
   humming in the dark; artist Macintosh Plus / vaporwave; chips Serial Experiments Lain, liminal spaces, vaporwave.
   primary #3db2b2 secondary #dad59e accent #d658cc bg #081111 surface #121d1d border #2a3535 text #e7f1f0 muted #97a9a8.
   heading 'VT323' (set 42px to match optical size), body 'IBM Plex Sans'. radius base 8px, xl 16px. density minimal. edge soft.

## Timeline (8.0s, loop seamless: frame at 8.0 == frame at 0.0)
- Three fittings, ~2.67s each, in order cyber → night → liminal → (loop to cyber).
- Each fitting holds ~1.9s, then a **snip transition** (~0.7s): a dashed red thread line draws diagonally across the

For Moss, I'm picturing a field-notes herbarium catalog with illustrated specimens and growth stats; for Ren, a dense night-market POS board with menu grids, prices, queue numbers, and neon Dela Gothic accents; for Ada, a sparse archive viewer with VHS scanlines, VT323 type, and dashed borders.

Really the core idea should be "one interface, cut three times" — the same collection screen structure (title, intro, primary action, item list, status) should persist, but density, edge style, type, and texture shift the layout architecture itself, not just colors and fonts. Right now the layouts are too similar aside from surface styling, which reads as a sloppy recolor rather than a true adaptation.

The Garment component also appears in Studio's fitting tab, specimen route, and conversation attachments, so any redesign needs to handle arbitrary personas generated by the token engine, not just the hero case. Since the aesthetic profile axes are enumerated, the layout archetype approach generalizes well — upgrading Garment itself to be axis-driven would improve Studio too, though there's risk of breaking existing layouts. I think that's still the right direction: the same underlying pattern applies to every persona, only the axis values differ.

I'm also noticing the current presentation looks a bit busy — the pinked fabric background and pin heads clip sloppily over the card's rounded corners, and the overall staging feels cluttered. A cleaner approach would be an artboard/canvas presentation with measurement annotations, since designers tend to appreciate spec-style redlines.

Thinking through the "tailor's atelier" concept more, the hero currently hides measurements, but adding a redline annotation layer with chalk-blue dimension lines for padding, radius, type specs, and color swatches would feel like Figma's dev mode inspect, which designers would really respond to. I'm sketching a hero layout with text and a CTA on the left, and on the right a "fitting table" showing the persona's interface specimen staged on a pattern-paper cutting mat.

The persona switcher could show small portrait tags with labels like "Moss · Cyberbotanist" tying the hero into the conversation below, with each persona getting its own carefully designed screen — Moss's being warm, organic, hand-drawn, built around a "field notes" specimen collection in Fraunces type.

Next I'd want Ren, a "night market coder" persona with a more maximalist, geometric, snappy feel using Dela Gothic One type and noisy textures.

For his dashboard, I'm picturing a dense grid board with a bold heading, a marquee ticker of keywords, and 6-8 tiles for spaces with big mono numbers, plus a compact "now playing" bar with neon outlines and tight hairline-bordered 4px radii.

Then there's Ada, the "liminal weeb" persona — cooler, minimal, asymmetric, with VT323 retro type, liquid motion, and a grainy VHS-like aesthetic; her UI would lean sparse with lots of negative space, an off-left heading, and a single featured artifact styled like a scanlined VHS frame.

Now I'm thinking through how to generalize this into a system: tying layout archetypes to density (sparse/layered/board) and letting layoutStyle (organic, grid, asymmetric, editorial, brutalist) modify radii, borders, and spacing, while iconStyle swaps the same icon set between line, filled, hand-drawn, geometric, and abstract renderings via different SVG techniques. This feels like a solid, generative design framework worth building out fully.

I also want to rethink the hero's presentation stage, swapping the pink cloth and clipped pins for a cleaner cutting-mat artboard with chalk-blue redline annotations, keeping the tailor identity but fixing the pins so they sit properly on the mat holding a tag rather than clipping over card corners. The redesigned cards need to come first since the video should showcase them.

My plan: first announce the work, then redesign the Garment persona specimen and hero stage, verifying with screenshots across all three personas on desktop and mobile, and checking the Studio fitting tab, specimen page, and conversation attachment still render correctly. After that, move to video production — capturing Playwright recordings of the landing page persona switches, conversation flows, Studio flows, and the /method page, then generating narration and persona dialogue via fal using ElevenLabs multilingual voices, keeping continuity with the existing tour's "Aria" voice.

I'm also considering adding talking-head clips for each persona delivering an in-character line via Veo3 fast image-to-video with audio as the "wow" factor, plus a subtle ambient music bed from ElevenLabs. Then I'd assemble everything into a 16:9 HyperFrames composition around 90 seconds with captions, embed it on the landing page's "See it in use" section and the docs Studio guide, and should check whether the existing product-launch-video workflow skill covers this website-capture approach — leaning toward a video that both sells the "why" and demonstrates the "what it's like to use it" through captured screens, likely around 90 seconds to two minutes long.

I'll settle on roughly 100 seconds for the site embed at 16:9, favoring the automation path through the product-launch-video workflow even though it may involve heavy machinery like capture and scripting — I should read through the workflow once installed to confirm. I need to keep narration voice consistent with "Aria" from the previous Studio guide run, check git status without committing anything unprompted, and quickly review how the companion/voice work integrated talking loops before giving the user a brief status update and diving into tool calls.
I'll start by redesigning the three hero persona cards, then create a narrated demo video using fal (voice narration and images cost just cents, while talking clips run about $1 each).
